application_guidance.input_pattern: A pair of points passed through the same Hilbert-space resolvent with the same positive parameter.
read_original_when: Replacing the Hilbert norm by a general Banach geometry or using approximate rather than exact resolvent images.
sensitive_conditions: The two images use the same T and c.
The norm and inner product are those of H.
Maximality supplies global resolvent existence; monotonicity supplies the inequality.

content.intended_use: Supply the precise resolvent inequality used in the criterion (A) convergence Proof.

dependencies: Resolvent existence on H is the source-stated maximal-monotonicity fact on printed p.878; its external Minty citation was not independently read.
proofs.locator: PDF p.5 / printed p.881, Proposition 1(a–c) and complete Proof; existence premise at PDF p.2 / printed p.878 before Eq.(1.6)
map: Part (a) follows from Q=I-P and the defining resolvent inclusion z-P(z) in cT(P(z)).
Apply monotonicity to c^(-1)Q(z) in T(P(z)) and c^(-1)Q(z') in T(P(z')); multiplying by c>0 gives part (b).
Write z-z'=(P(z)-P(z'))+(Q(z)-Q(z')). Expand the squared norm. Its cross term is nonnegative by part (b), proving part (c).
proofs.omitted_details: No algebraic step of the short Proposition 1 Proof is omitted from the map. This does not reprove the cited general resolvent existence theorem.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually viewed the relevant original-page derivatives for PDF pp.2 and 5 and read the Proposition 1 statement and complete short Proof. The map is a faithful expanded paraphrase of that source Proof, not a new local Theorem.

assumptions: T is maximal monotone on the real Hilbert space H.
c is a strictly positive real number; no nonempty-zero-set assumption is needed.
statement.conclusion: (a) z=P(z)+Q(z) and c^(-1)Q(z) in T(P(z)) for every z. (b) <P(z)-P(z'),Q(z)-Q(z')> >= 0 for every z,z'. (c) ||P(z)-P(z')||^2+||Q(z)-Q(z')||^2 <= ||z-z'||^2 for every z,z'. In the paper c=c_k and P=P_k, Q=Q_k for each k.
statement.objects_and_definitions: H is a real Hilbert space, T:H -> 2^H is maximal monotone, c>0, P=(I+cT)^(-1), Q=I-P. The source's resolvent existence fact makes P single-valued on all H.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such H,T,c and every z,z' in H. There is no randomness.

research_use.reason: The nonnegative cross term yields a squared-distance bound with an explicit complementary residual.

summary: For a maximal monotone operator on a real Hilbert space, its resolvent and complementary mapping satisfy the decomposition, graph inclusion and squared-distance inequality of Proposition 1(a–c), without assuming a zero exists.
title: Resolvent decomposition and firm nonexpansiveness
use_when: Control resolvent distances and complementary residuals in a Hilbert-space argument.
